newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan seeks only unleaded reformate for Jan 1-15.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seeks only unleaded reformate for Jan 1-15.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is seeking only unleaded reformate in its import tender for January 1-15 delivery, a CPC official said on Tuesday.
"We are phasing out leaded gasoline, so imports will gradually be decreased," the official said.
Although Taiwan's government has targetted the total phase out of leaded gasoline by 2000, it wants to move towards cleaner gasoline as soon as possible, she said.
"Unleaded gasoline is already taking a greater market share ... around 70 percent," the official said. "It is hoped it (the phase out) can be sooner than expected."
CPC is seeking only 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane unleaded reformate for January 1-15 delivery, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung or Taichung.
The tender closes on November 25 and offers will be valid for two days.

In its December purchases, CPC paid less than $25.50 a barrel, c-and-f Taiwan, for a 250,000-barrel cargo of leaded reformate and slightly more than $25.50 for two 250,000-barrel-cargoes of unleaded 95-octane reformate for December 16-31 deliveries.
